body:
Parent: [#6018](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/6018) (Atlas ingestion program). Statements S7–S10 of the 2026-11-04 brief.

## Questions (Drew, in substance)

1. **Where do agent notes go?** Agents produce notes constantly (working notes, research_notes, goal files, memory entries, scratch findings). There is no single placement rule today, and the answer decides what Atlas ingests and what future agents can find.
2. **What is the difference between the Zettelkasten and the repo** as note homes? (Drew's dictation says "that tile cast" — read as the Zettelkasten, dezren39/zettel, the Emanote slip-box; interpretation recorded in the program inventory.) When does a note belong in the zettel graph vs committed to a code repo vs kept in agent memory/workspace?
3. **Publishing directly into the ID graph**: some notes/objects should be published as ID-graph objects rather than files at all — which classes, and what changes (identity, writer-set, relations) when they are?

## Tie-ins (do not reinvent)

- ID relation methods are already covered elsewhere: writer-set authority [#5545](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/5545), the capability/relation family under [#5686](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/5686), and tonight's worlds/licensing program ([#5955](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/5955)). This design **consumes** those relation methods for notes rather than inventing a parallel model.
- Tonight's zettel brain-dump design already fixes part of the shape: every surface emits ONE `note_submission` envelope; zettel notes are first-class Atlas corpus; the Turso submission DB is the system of record; mandatory metadata = content hash + provenance spans; nothing auto-commits (staging → human promotion). The placement design must compose with that pipeline, not bypass it.
- The docs migration ([#5981](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/5981) + [#5983](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/5983)) is moving the canonical home of fleet/architecture docs into code — placement rules for agent notes must agree with the migration's classification standard (sandbox-environment material stays in hatch-personal; everything else canonicalizes to code / zettel / ID).
- Atlas ingestion (parent program) is the downstream consumer: whatever homes are chosen, each needs an ingestion path with provenance marks (source system @ machine @ date).

## Design must answer

- A placement decision table: note class (ephemeral working note, durable finding, design, research, daily log, user-facing doc) → home (workspace scratch / memory / repo doc / zettel / ID graph) → lifetime → Atlas-ingested? at which tier?
- The zettel-vs-repo distinction stated crisply enough that an agent mid-task can apply it in one step.
- The ID-graph publishing path: which note classes qualify, what an ID-native note's identity/provenance is, and how repo/zettel copies relate to it (canonical vs projection).
- Migration expectations for the existing sprawl (research_notes, goal workspaces, memory topics): swept, grandfathered, or left with pointers.

## Done looks like

A placement design doc + the decision table, cross-linked from the zettel program and the ID epic ([#2056](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/2056)), with any implementation split into follow-on issues.
